summary: The study describes the Atomic Layer Epitaxy (ALE) growth of silicon (Si) using alternate pulses of SiCl2H2 and H2 at temperatures near 500°C. The process involves self-limiting growth with fine control over film thickness without Ge out-diffusion. The model explains the observed plateaus in growth rate versus pressure or temperature, and the study also examines the use of atomic hydrogen (H2) and chlorosilanes for Si ALE.
evidence: We deposited Si on Ge(100) via alternate pulses of SiCl2H2 and Si,H2 with T, near 500°C and characterized the very thin Si layers. The amount of Si grown was measured by medium energy ion scattering (MEIS), and was proportional to the number of growth cycles as shown in Fig. 3. This process resembles ALE growth, but is not self-limiting. The growth T controlled the Si morphology, as seen by XTEM and by incident angle scans in TOF-DR studies.
